public_rationale: There is substantial evidence of earlier NVIDIA-chip diversion into China. That supports taking the allegation seriously, but the accessible records do not establish the ongoing sales chain in the selected reporting period. They also do not settle whether NVIDIA knowingly participated. The company's denial does not disprove diversion.
limitations: The speaker did not specify a reporting period; the October convention materially limits this assessment.
An assessment of historical downstream diversion would be broader than this assessment of the ongoing claim.
The cited complaint records allegations and responses, not adjudicated facts.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: NVIDIA is selling GPUs to China through proxies and shell corporations.

statement.excerpt: It’s impossible to argue that NVIDIA is not selling GPUs to China through a web of proxies and shell corporations — and now the only real questions are how much, to whom, and when.

from_speaker: NVIDIA is ... selling GPUs to China
through a web of proxies and shell corporations
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that NVIDIA-origin GPU sales reach Chinese buyers through intermediaries that conceal the ultimate destination.
Diversion by intermediaries does not by itself establish NVIDIA management's knowledge or participation.
For this ongoing, nonfinancial observation, use October 2026, the latest complete calendar month before publication. The speaker supplies no reporting period.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable shipment, ownership, invoice or investigative records trace NVIDIA GPU sales through proxy or shell buyers to Chinese end users during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Affirmative, sufficiently comprehensive records disprove the alleged sales routes during the target period. Company denials or unsuccessful investigations alone are insufficient.
